candidates.rich_summary: Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Red Wind, Coral Worlds’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by recipients of the Art Jameel Curatorial Open Call, Huda Tayob and Miriam Hillawi Abraham. Red Wind, Coral Worlds sites the Red Sea within an expanded and interconnected oceanic terrain. The exhibition traces the entangled worlds that converge across its waters, attending to the material and affective remnants left in the wake of centuries of movement and migration shaped by trade, pilgrimage, and displacement. The works in the exhibition act as navigational systems – maps that negotiate arrival and loss, and offerings that recall forgotten pasts. Drawing on familial and communal archives, they speak to ongoing waves of disruption and continuity.

candidates.rich_summary: Opening May 20, 2026, ‘Global Positioning System’ is an upcoming exhibition curated by Indranjan Banerjee and Lucas Morin. Global Positioning System is an exhibition dedicated to mapping and navigation systems. It tells stories of fast cars and slow trains, street barriers and trembling grounds, warping highways and broken bridges. Gathering over forty artists across Art Jameel’s two centres in Jeddah and Dubai, the exhibition presents a wide range of artistic practices—from research-based engagements with infrastructure projects to conceptual works that question the very perception of distance. Maps, remaining the dominant representation space, carry a heavy weight. Far from reflecting geography objectively, they are instruments of power that embody specific worldviews. Though based on mapping, navigation systems like GPS render traditional maps redundant; they reduce navigation to an abstract exercise and remove the need to comprehend the physical space one moves through.

candidates.title: Buraydah International Dates Carnival
candidates.summary: Discover Buraydah International Dates Carnival, one of Saudi’s leading date festivals, taking place at Dates City in Buraydah from 1 August to 15 October 2026. The carnival brings together daily date auctions with cultural and heritage experiences that celebrate the date palm and its agricultural legacy. It features the Palm Centre, auction and market areas, and an accompanying events tent, alongside specialised exhibitions, traditional crafts, the Palm Museum, interactive broadcasting platforms, hospitality areas, and food trucks, all reflecting Buraydah’s identity and agricultural heritage.

candidates.title: Continuum '26 Diriyah Art Futures Emerging New Media Artists Programme
candidates.summary: Discover Continuum '26, the second edition of the annual exhibition series celebrating the creative outcomes of participants in the Emerging New Media Artists Programme at Diriyah Art Futures. The exhibition showcases the results of a year-long development journey during which 16 artists explored new approaches to creative practice, production, and meaning-making. The works range from immersive and multimedia installations to virtual reality, artificial intelligence, light, sound, and moving-image works. The experience goes beyond viewing the artworks, with a program of activities accompanying the exhibition, including talks, hands-on workshops, and masterclasses that offer an opportunity to discover different aspects and practices of new media art.

candidates.rich_summary: Join the Jameel Library for a wide range of programmes led by community members this September! You could also pitch your own programme here . Writing Circle: Writing Against the Algorithm with Hassan Alshiyoukh September 4, 2026 5-8pm What does it mean to write honestly in an age built for speed, performance, and manufactured opinion? Join Hassan Alshiyoukh in a workshop exploring the personal essay as a space where complexity is welcomed, contradictions are embraced, and the slow work of self-discovery takes precedence over the curated self. Through close readings of acclaimed essayists, guided writing exercises, and peer and instructor feedback, participants will move from observation to reflection, learning to ask not just “what happened?” but “what does it mean and why does it matter?” Together, participants will trace how personal experience becomes literary non-fiction: identifying compelling subjects in everyday life, developing a central guiding question, shaping memory...

candidates.summary: Echoes of the Familiar exhibition explores the concept that home transcends mere physical space, embodying a tapestry of memories intricately woven into its very walls. It is within these confines that the echoes of laughter from childhood games intermingle with the remnants of disagreements and tears shed upon pillows. The scent of maternal cooking and the rhythmic snoring of a father create a comforting ambiance, while the presence of a grandmother before the television grounds us in familial continuity. These shared experiences resonate universally, forging a collective nostalgia for "al zaman al Jameel

candidates.image_alt: Hayy Sounds | Listening Stations, Part of the Exhibition ‘Red Wind, Coral Worlds’
candidates.rich_summary: Sound forms an integral element of ‘Red Wind, Coral Worlds’, an exhibition curated by Huda Tayob and Miriam Hillawi Abraham , recipients of the Art Jameel Curatorial Open Call 2025–2026. As part of the exhibition’s closing programme, Hayy Sounds presents a series of listening stations along with a photographic display, in collaboration with Frequency Room, that explores the vast and often underrepresented sonic histories, practices and encounters extending across the expansive geographies and entanglements of the Red Sea. Like the red wind, sound offers an alternative mapping of geographic and urban space: a temporal residue that can be felt, heard and carried across distance, borders and generations. It moves through ports, coastlines, cities and rural landscapes, carried by migration, memory and exchange. Existing alongside oral history, sound also retains a certain opacity — something that cannot always be fully translated, traced or contained.

The event brings together the third editions of the Global Forum on Connecting the World from the Skies and the Space Sustainability Forum, creating a global platform to advance innovation in non-terrestrial networks (NTN) and promote the sustainable use of space. It will convene policymakers, regulators, industry leaders, researchers, and technology experts to discuss the future of space communications, integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial connectivity, space sustainability, and emerging opportunities in the global space economy. The three-day programme will feature keynote sessions, panel discussions, technical presentations, and the announcement of the winners of the third NTN International Research Competition, highlighting the latest developments in space communications, international collaboration, and sustainable space technologies.

candidates.title: World Stadiums and Arenas Summit
candidates.summary: The World Stadiums and Arenas Summit—the region’s largest stadiums and sports facilities conference and exhibition—returns to Riyadh at Hilton Riyadh Hotel & Residences. This flagship gathering brings together global leaders, architects, developers, government stakeholders, and sports federations to showcase cutting-edge technologies, sustainable design solutions, and best practices in building and upgrading stadiums and sports venues. With Saudi Vision 2030 driving major investment in sports and entertainment infrastructure, the summit offers a front-row view of the latest industry trends—from smart stadiums to eco-friendly facilities—and how they are shaping the future of sport in the Kingdom and beyond. Register Now World Sports 360 Summit | Athlete 360 Co-located with the World Stadiums and Arenas Summit, World Sports 360 Summit | Athlete 360, brings together global experts, elite athletes, coaches, and industry leaders to shape the future of sports, wellness, and human performance in the Kingdom. Focused on integrating performance and health, the programme spotlights cutting-edge performance optimisation (recovery, data-driven training, and advanced technology), holistic athlete development (nutrition, sports medicine, mental resilience, and long-term wellbeing), and the evolving Saudi sports landscape powered by Vision 2030. Expect practical insights, knowledge exchange, and forward-looking discussions spanning the sports economy, club management, revenue strategies, talent development and scouting, and the latest innovations in athlete technology and performance. Register Now The programme also features the World Stadiums and Arenas Awards , celebrating standout achievements in stadium and arena development across 10 categories highlighting innovation, sustainability, and exceptional project delivery—including architectural design for new venues, renovation and modernisation, innovative materials, multi-use design, creative lighting, eco-friendly architecture, community and social impact, safety and security leadership, accessibility and inclusivity initiatives, and the People’s Choice Award for outstanding stadium design.

candidates.title: Global Health Exhibition
candidates.summary: Global Health Exhibition 2026 takes place in Riyadh on 26–29 October 2026 at the Riyadh Exhibition and Convention Center (Malham) under the theme “Invest in Health,” bringing together global healthcare leaders, decision-makers, investors, and innovators to shape the next era of health. The event spotlights the trends and partnerships accelerating digital transformation and new models of care—from AI in clinical practice and digital health to workforce evolution and breakthrough medical technologies—through a major exhibition and multi-stage conference programme. candidates.title: New Global Sport Conference

The program reflects GASTAT's ongoing efforts to strengthen the Kingdom's position in the statistical field and support the development of data and statistical systems in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and Saudi Vision 2030. In 1798, Napoleon lands his army in Egypt, defeats the Mameluke warlords (the remnants of Ottoman rule), and reaches Cairo. Three brothers, Egyptian patriots, chafe under Mameluke rule and reject the prospect of French domination. Bakr, the eldest, is a hothead, quick to advocate armed rebellion; Ali is more philosophical and poetic while Yehia is young and impressionable.

candidates.image_alt: Hayy Cinema | Youssef Chahine Retrospective: Alexandria, Why? (1979)
candidates.rich_summary: OPENING FILM Alexandria Why / Iskindereya Leh Director: Youssef Chahine Release Date: 1978 Running Time: 120min Language: Arabic Subtitles: English Alexandria, Why? Marked a radical, newly introspective turn in Chahine’s active career, a sharp departure from his Fifties musicals and melodramas and his later epics and political films. The first of a semi-autobiographical tetralogy, entitled “Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man,” Alexandria, Why? focuses on a precocious adolescent whose dreams and colorful attempts to become an actor unfold against the vivid backdrop of Alexandria during World War II. A rich cast inspires Chahine’s young thespian hero with a wealth of dramatic sub-plots – at turns hilarious and touching – about wartime life. The autobiographical nature and nostalgic flavour of Alexandria, Why? make it one of Chahine’s most accessible works, a charming and entertaining film that also delivers a potently subversive and impassioned anti-war message. candidates.title: AlUla Tour
candidates.organizer: Royal Commission for AlUla / Experience AlUla
candidates.summary: AlUla Tour is a major fixture on the international cycling calendar, attracting the world’s top teams and riders for a multi-stage race through one of the most spectacular landscapes on Earth. From dramatic desert backdrops to iconic landmarks like Maraya and the Oasis, each stage delivers high performance and unforgettable scenery in equal measure. Individual AlUla Tour stages will be announced closer to the race date, but previous editions have seen riders traverse routes from Old Town to Harrat Uwayrid and Winter Park to Wirkah Mountain.

candidates.title: Hayy Cinema | Hayy Classics: An Experience from Jeddah's Past
candidates.summary: Hayy Classics: An Experience from Jeddah’s Past Join us at Hayy Cinema for a nostalgic experience of Jeddah’s cinematic and cultural past. Relive the charm of outdoor cinemas as we showcase classic films on a 35mm projector under the stars at Saha. Outdoor cinemas first emerged in Jeddah in the early 1960s, bringing communities together to enjoy a vibrant mix of international and Arab films. In addition to the screenings, join us for related workshops and panel discussions.

candidates.title: 24th ERRA Annual Conference
candidates.summary: The 24th ERRA Annual Conference takes place in Riyadh from February 1 to 3, bringing together international regulators, experts, and industry leaders to discuss the future of electricity sector governance and transformation. Hosted by the Saudi Electricity Regulatory Authority (SERA), the conference is held under the theme “From Oversight to Foresight: The Proactive Regulator in the Electricity Transformation.” The conference explores forward-looking regulatory approaches, innovation in electricity markets, consumer protection, and evolving energy systems. It also reflects Riyadh’s growing role as a destination for major international forums and supports the Kingdom’s wider ambitions in energy leadership and sustainable development. Registration

candidates.title: Human Capability Initiative Conference
candidates.venue: King Abdulaziz International Conference Center (KAICC), Riyadh
candidates.summary: Under the patronage of His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince, Prime Minister, and Chairman of the Human Capability Development Program (HCDP) Committee, the third edition of the Human Capability Initiative (HCI) Conference—one of the Saudi Vision 2030 Realization Programs—will take place on April 12–13, 2027, at the King Abdulaziz International Conference Center in Riyadh under the theme “The Human Code.” The conference will focus on three pillars: deep human connection, sound reasoning amid complexity, and value-driven creation to safeguard human contribution and purpose in the age of accelerated technological advancement. HCI 2027 aims to attract more than 15,000 visitors and over 250 local and international speakers, including policymakers, thought leaders, and experts from government, private, nonprofit, and global institutions, providing a platform to exchange best practices and showcase inspiring global success stories. The United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland will participate as Country of Honor, reflecting the strength of the Saudi-British strategic partnership in advancing human capability development. Building on the success of previous editions—which welcomed over 23,000 visitors, featured 550+ speakers, and announced more than 156 launches and agreements—the conference reinforces the Kingdom’s commitment to investing in human potential as a foundation for sustainable growth and global competitiveness in alignment with Saudi Vision 2030.
